newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber steady to higher, tight supply - trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber steady to higher, tight supply - trade.

text.p: Tighter supplies continued to support Thai rubber prices this week while buying was modest, trade sources said on Friday.
China was absent from the market, while there was some pre-holiday buying from Japan, they told Reuters.
"The tight supply could continue well into January due to this unseasonably long monsoon in the south," said Sucharit Promdej of Rubber Research Institute.
"Tapping activity dropped substantially because of the rains," he said.

Only 45,942 kg of sheet rubbers entered the market this week, a 9.77 percent drop from last week. During the same period last year, more than 100,000 kg of sheets of rubber went into the market, according to auction market sources.
The benchmark RSS3 for January shipment was quoted around US$1.25-1.26 a kg FOB Bangkok compared with $1.24-1.25 last week, traders said.
The drop in supplies also pushed latex prices up to $0.94-0.95 a kg from 0.94 last week, they said.
